svg.aria-label: How to write 岛: 7 strokes · 6 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing 岛
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 岛 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 岛.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%B2%9B.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 岛, in two pieces. Medians 1–4 draw the top: a short left-falling stroke, a small horizontal that turns down and hooks to the left without lifting, a dot inside it, then a stroke that runs down the left side, turns right along the foot, turns down again and hooks to the left without lifting. Medians 5–7 draw 山 as 山 is written alone: the middle vertical, the left side that turns right along the foot without lifting, then the right vertical. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions, the turns, the hooks and six intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
